newsitem.title: USA: Turner apologizes for Murdoch "Fuhrer" remark.
newsitem.headline: Turner apologizes for Murdoch "Fuhrer" remark.

text.p: Cable News Network founder Ted Turner, who is fighting a business battle with fellow media tycoon Rupert Murdoch, apologised for comparing his rival to Adolf Hitler, a civil rights group said on Wednesday.

The Anti-Defamation League (ADL), an organisation that counters anti-Semitism and other forms of bigotry, had written to Turner saying that such a comparison "trivializes a profound historical tragedy" -- the millions of Jewish victims of Nazism under Hitler's Germany.
In his response to ADL national director Abraham Foxman, Turner wrote, "I hope you and all those offended by this comment will accept my deepest apology."

At issue between Turner and Murdoch was whether Time Warner, the nation's second largest cable operator, will carry Murdoch's soon to be launched competitor to CNN, which is becoming part of the Time Warner empire.

Murdoch plans to launch his 24-hour-a-day cable news channel, the Fox News Channel, on Oct. 7. He has billed it as a conservative alternative to what he perceives as Turner's liberal CNN, an operation he has often said he wanted to buy and make the centrepiece of a global media empire.
Last Thursday, Turner accused Murdoch of using his newspapers as weapons in a media war. He told reporters, "Talking to Murdoch is like confronting the late Fuhrer."
The New York-based ADL said Turner wrote Foxman that he realised his words were "unfortunate" and "offensive".

According to the ADL, Turner said his comparison referred "only to the way Hitler managed the news in Germany. It was not intended to offend nor to trivialise the role of an individual who wreaked so much havoc upon the Jewish people."
